column2: Five fused benzene rings, found in soot, cigarette smoke and burnt toast. In 1933 it was isolated from coal tar as a cause of the cancers in chimney sweeps first described in 1775.

Sixty carbon atoms in a football of 20 hexagons and 12 pentagons, discovered in 1985. Everyone thinks they're the clever one for saying it, and chemists still argue whether its hexagons count as benzene rings.
